name: rigid-movable-boundary
title: Rung 2 · Rigid movable boundary
claim: OBSERVED: a drag-loaded movable wall settles to a non-zero velocity. Whether the stall force stays within the Peskin-1993 bound is NOT yet checked.
decision_figure: force–velocity phase portrait, low-drag vs high-drag on shared axes, with transient/steady-state windows marked and the Peskin stall bound drawn
expected_pattern: velocity settles to a non-zero steady state; force and drag balance; stall force ≤ Peskin ceiling
acceptance_threshold: steady-state mean barrier_velocity in (0, Peskin ceiling]
question: With barrier_kind="rigid_movable", does the wall translate at a velocity proportional to the mean contact force (drag-balance Peskin 1993 setup), and does the stall force remain bounded?

purpose.question: With barrier_kind="rigid_movable", does the wall translate at a velocity proportional to the mean contact force (drag-balance Peskin 1993 setup), and does the stall force remain bounded?
purpose.mechanism: The wall obeys dz/dt = F/drag while staying planar (no deformation). Same actin model as the fixed-boundary rung; only the barrier's response changes.
purpose.expected_outcome: barrier_velocity stabilizes at a non-zero value over the second half of the run; stall force ≤ Peskin closed-form upper bound at this drag.

variants.name: low-drag
variants.description: Light wall — faster barrier velocity, lower stall force.

variants.name: high-drag
variants.description: Heavy wall — approaches the Peskin stall regime.

tests.name: stall-force-within-peskin-bound
tests.question: Mean barrier_velocity over the second half is positive (wall is moving) and below the zero-load Peskin velocity ceiling.

modified_processes: BrownianRatchetCoupler: integrate barrier_z via dz/dt = F/drag while keeping the wall planar.
model_change.notes: Spec §2.2 rung 2. Same actin model as rung 1; wall now translates under integrated contact force per Peskin 1993.

simulation_set.name: rung2-rigid-movable
simulation_set.description: Single closed-loop run; wall translates under drag balance with the actin contact force.

mechanism_uncertainty_addressed: Does a drag-loaded movable barrier exhibit load-dependent stalling within the Peskin (1993) bound?
resolved_uncertainties: A movable wall settles to a non-zero steady velocity (8/8 runs, OBSERVED).
remaining_uncertainties: Stall force vs the Peskin closed-form ceiling is unchecked; barrier_drag is recorded for only 2/8 runs so the drag sweep is not separable.

alternate_hypotheses.statement: Steady velocity reflects the imposed drag balance (dz/dt=F/drag) rather than ratchet-limited advance.
evidence_for: velocity tracks 1/drag by construction in the two tagged runs.
evidence_against: a Peskin-consistent stall force at high drag would indicate genuine load-dependent ratcheting.

mechanism_update_proposals.statement: Adds a drag-balance stalling regime between the fixed wall and the flexible membrane.

followup_study_proposals.title: Drag sweep with barrier_drag recorded in run params + Peskin stall-bound overlay
followup_study_proposals.expected_information_gain: Separates the low/high-drag conditions and tests the stall force against theory.
